question: What CGPA does an undergraduate need to stay off academic warning?
expected_answer: 2.00 CGPA. If a student's CGPA falls below 2.00 at the end of any semester (summer included) a warning is issued and the warning count goes up by one. Evidence confirmed: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf, section 5.4, PDF page 24 (printed page 18). Also consistent with grading-page.html (Warning/Probation table, BBA/BS 2.0) and Prospectus 2026 item 11. I found no mismatch in the section label; the likely confusion is printed page numbers (footer) versus PDF page numbers, which differ by 6.

question: What happens to a student whose attendance falls below the required minimum in a course?
expected_answer: They become ineligible to sit the final exam of that course and are given an F/A grade (fail due to attendance shortage). Evidence confirmed: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf, section 1.22, PDF page 10; section 1.21 on the same page sets the 100% requirement with up to 20% absence condonable by the HoD for genuine reasons.

question: How is a student's CGPA calculated?
expected_answer: It's the credit-weighted average of grade points over all courses taken so far, across semesters. For repeated courses only the most recent grade counts, even if it is lower, and W grades don't affect it. Evidence confirmed: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf, section 2.6, PDF page 12 (credit weighting is in 2.4-2.5 on page 12; repeat rule 2.7 runs from page 12 to 13; W in 2.8 on page 13).

question: How many grade points does a B+ carry?
expected_answer: 3.33 grade points for BBA/BS (also 3.33 in the MBA/MS and PhD tables). Evidence confirmed: grading-page.html, Letter Code Interpretation, BBA & BS table, page 1, and consistent with academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf section 2.3, PDF page 12. Minor note: the web page labels B+ 'Very Good' while the handbook says 'Good'; the points are the same.

question: What is the tuition fee refund timeline when a student withdraws from the university?
review_verdict: Keep, but tighten the wording to say tuition fee.
expected_answer: Tuition fee is refunded by how many days after classes commence: 100% up to day 10, 80% up to day 15, 60% up to day 20, 50% up to day 30, and nothing from day 31 (days include weekends and holidays). Admission fee is never refundable, and the security deposit is refundable at completion of degree or closing of admission. Evidence confirmed: fee-structure-page.html, Fee Refund Policy, page 1. Withdrawing from an individual course gets no fee refund (academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf 4.22, PDF page 22).

question: What does the Student Handbook say about using generative AI in assignments?

5. Unacceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools
4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools
4. Acceptable Uses of Generative AI Tools

expected_answer: Short version: AI can help with research, summarising and organising, but it isn't a source and you can't submit AI-generated work as your own; any AI content used must be quoted and referenced. Generating a whole assignment, or using paraphrasing tools to disguise work, counts as misconduct, and staff may use Turnitin's AI score. In non-lab courses AI is allowed and sometimes encouraged for assignments, but every assignment must carry a quiz or demonstration that holds most of the marks (submission is typically 10-15%). Corrected evidence: student-handbook-jun-2026.pdf, section 5 starts on PDF page 52 but runs to pages 53-54; also section 4 (PDF pages 50-52), section 6.1 (PDF page 56) and the plagiarism item on PDF page 13.

question: What is the purpose of the Faculty Entrepreneurship and Technical Start-ups Policy?
expected_answer: It sets out the guidelines for full-time NUCES faculty to take part in technical, innovative start-ups that commercialise research done at NUCES campuses. Faculty entrepreneurship covers founding or managing a start-up, holding significant equity, sitting on its governing board, or receiving a share of its revenue. Evidence confirmed: faculty-entrepreneurship-and-technical-start-ups-policy.pdf, section 1 Purpose (1.1-1.2), PDF page 1.

My CGPA has dropped below 2.00 for a second time and I'm now on my 2nd academic warning. Can I register for a course I haven't taken before next semester?
author: nofalzaman
expected_answer: Not on your own. A student on the 2nd academic warning must not register for a new course unless the Head of Department recommends it and the Controller of Examinations approves it. In practice you'd be repeating courses instead (F-grade courses are compulsory, D/D+/C- ones are recommended).
difficulty_reason: Ordinary. One rule (4.4(e)) answers it directly, with no need to combine documents.
source_notes: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | section 4.4(e), Registration of Students under Academic Warning | PDF page 20 (printed page 14).

question: I have a really bad cold on the day of my midterm. Will the university let me apply for a retake?
author: itsmeaounmuhammad-boop
expected_answer: Most likely not. Coughs and colds are listed among the cases where retake applications will not be considered. Retakes are meant for things like hospitalization, a death in the immediate family, severe injury, or high fever/diarrhea/asthma backed by a medical certificate, with documents submitted on Flex within the deadline. The Campus Committee and Director have the final say.
difficulty_reason: Ordinary. The retake policy section answers it directly, with the exclusion listed in one place.
source_notes: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | section 9, Policy on Retake Examination (cases considered, cases not considered, Notes) | PDF pages 37-38 (the cough and cold exclusion is on page 38).

question: I got a 3.85 SGPA this semester but I withdrew from one course. Can I still get one of the top-three semester position medals?
author: nofalzaman
expected_answer: No. To be eligible for the semester position medal a student must not have failed, repeated or withdrawn from any course that semester. They must also have passed the full prescribed load and earned at least 3.00. Registering for fewer or more credit hours than the specified total rules you out as well. The withdrawal alone disqualifies you, however high the SGPA is.
difficulty_reason: Ordinary. Rule 7.10(b) answers it directly, with 7.11 as a supporting condition in the same section.
source_notes: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | sections 7.10(a)-(d) and 7.11, Top three position holders in bachelor's degree programs | PDF page 32 (heading 7.10 begins on page 31).

question: Can I use ChatGPT in my Data Structures lab, and if the lab instructor does allow it, how does the lab change?
author: itsmeaounmuhammad-boop
expected_answer: By default, no. AI tools are prohibited in labs such as PF, OOP and DS unless the lab instructor explicitly allows them, and only about 10% of labs are meant to allow it. When it is allowed, the session runs to 2.5 hours, the last half hour is a small quiz done on your own without AI, and you hand in the prompts you used. Marks come from the quiz result and the quality of your prompts.
difficulty_reason: Ordinary. All of it is stated in one subsection (6.2), so no cross-document reasoning is needed.
source_notes: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | section 10 (Policy on Generative AI Based Tools), 6.2 Use in Lab Courses | PDF page 50 (printed page 44).

question: I'm graduating next summer and still need one elective I've never taken. Can I take it as a new course in the summer semester?
author: nofalzaman
expected_answer: Under the current rules, no. Summer is only for repeat courses (for students on academic warning I/II, graduating students, FYP-I eligibility, or unlocking a Fall course via a prerequisite). No new courses are allowed in any of those categories, and you can only repeat courses you registered in before and received a letter grade for, up to a maximum of 2. The Aug 2023 rules had an exception allowing one or two new electives to graduate, but that edition is superseded; both the June 2026 handbook and Prospectus 2026 say repeat courses only.
difficulty_reason: Hard. The answer needs the current 2026 handbook and prospectus to be combined, and the older 2023 exception has to be recognised as superseded and ignored.
source_notes: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | sections 6.1-6.3 and 6.6 | PDF page 28; prospectus-2026-academic-rules-and-regulations.pdf | item 19, Rules for Summer Semester | PDF page 3; undergraduate-academic-rules-aug-2023.pdf | section 6.4(iii) | PDF page 20 (superseded, for contrast only).

question: I only attended 75% of the classes in one course this semester. Can I still sit the final exam, and what would show on my transcript?
author: itsmeaounmuhammad-boop
expected_answer: No. The handbook asks for 100% attendance and lets the HoD condone absence of at most 20% for genuine reasons such as illness, and the Prospectus states 80% as the undergraduate minimum. At 75% you are 25% absent, which is beyond what can be condoned. You'd be ineligible for the final exam and receive an F/A grade (fail due to shortage of attendance), which carries 0.00 grade points, the same as an F.
difficulty_reason: Hard. It combines the attendance rule, the 80% minimum from a different document, and the FA grade points from the grading page.
source_notes: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | sections 1.21-1.22 | PDF page 10, and section 2.2 | PDF page 11; prospectus-2026-academic-rules-and-regulations.pdf | item 1, Attendance Requirement | PDF page 1; grading-page.html | section 'The Following grades are common for all degree programs' (FA = 0.00) | page 1.

relevant.section: The Following grades are common for all degree programs

question: I think my final exam was marked wrongly. How much does a recheck cost, how long do I have to apply, and do I get the money back if my marks go up?
author: itsmeaounmuhammad-boop
expected_answer: A recheck costs Rs 500 per course or lab. You have to submit the prescribed form together with the fee so it reaches the Examination Office within seven days of the result announcement (you can apply even if you skipped the paper viewing session). The fee is refunded if your marks increase. The fee page says miscellaneous fees are non-refundable, but the academic rule on rechecking is the specific one, so the refund-on-increase applies.
difficulty_reason: Hard. The amount comes from the fee page while the deadline and refund come from the handbook, and the two documents appear to conflict on refunds.
source_notes: fee-structure-page.html | section Miscellaneous Fees (Paper Rechecking Fee, Per Course/Lab) | page 1; academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | sections 5.20-5.25, Rechecking of Final Exams | PDF pages 26-27.

question: I'm in my fifth semester and want to freeze my semester, but it's already the third week of classes. How many semesters can I freeze for and what will it cost?
author: nofalzaman
expected_answer: You can freeze for up to 2 semesters (only the first two semesters of a BS are excluded, so the fifth is fine). Because you're past the first two weeks of classes, the fee is the later rate of Rs 5,000 rather than Rs 2,000. Don't let it run past two consecutive semesters: the Prospectus lists failure to resume studies after freezing for two consecutive semesters as a ground for closing admission.
difficulty_reason: Hard. It combines the freeze limit from the handbook, the fee tier from the fee page and the closure consequence from the prospectus.
source_notes: academic-rules-handbook-jun-2026.pdf | section 4.18, Freezing of Semester | PDF page 22; fee-structure-page.html | section Miscellaneous Fees (Semester Freeze Fee; Late Registration/Freeze Fee after second week) | page 1; prospectus-2026-academic-rules-and-regulations.pdf | item 21 (PDF page 3) and item 25(b) (PDF page 4).
